the presence of CTC in blood is a strong indication of metastatic disease.
the presence of CTC in the blood stream can be used to determine the presence and spread of a cancer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to detect CTCs and cfDNA fragments in the blood of patients with breast cancer.

we have been able to detect circulating tumor cells and cell free DNA fragments in patients with cancer and have been able to identify the mutations that are present in the circulating tumor cells and cfDNA fragments.
the presence of CTC and cfDNA in the peripheral blood of patients with solid tumors is a potential marker for cancer prognosis and can be used to guide treatment.

liquid biopsies can be used to monitor the effectiveness of cancer therapies and can also be used to predict the outcome of a patient with cancer.
liquid biopsy can be a useful tool to detect the presence of cancer in a non invasive manner and to monitor the response of the cancer to treatment.
